newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-JOHNSON BACKS ROME BID FOR GAMES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-JOHNSON BACKS ROME BID FOR GAMES.

text.p: Double Olympic sprint gold medallist Michael Johnson gave his backing to Rome's bid for the 2004 Olympics on Tuesday, just days before the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announces a shortlist.
"It would be an ideal venue for the Olympics and I hope it gets the 2004 Games. I also like the people of this city a lot," the American told a news conference in Rome.
Johnson, who won the 200 and 400 metres titles at last year's Atlanta Olympics and also holds the world 200 metres record, was in Rome for one of his sponsors.
The IOC will announce a shortlist of five candidates for the Games in Lausanne on Friday and give its final choice on September 5. Rome and Athens are among the front-runners.
